questions.title: Where Can You Drop If You Go Back to Your Last Shot?
questions.question: If you can't play your ball and go back to where you last hit it, how close to that spot are you allowed to drop your ball?

choices.text: Right on the exact same spot
Within one club-length from that spot
Within two club-lengths from that spot

questions.explanation: You have to drop your ball within one club-length of where you played your last shot, and it can't be closer to the hole.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: This means your ball is in a tough spot you can't hit from. You get to choose what to do next.
This is how long your golf club is. You can use it to measure how far you can drop your ball.

questions.teachingTip: Let children measure out a club-length themselves so they know exactly how far they can drop the ball.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think they need to drop the ball right on the same spot where they last played, instead of anywhere within one club-length.
They might think they can drop anywhere they want nearby or even on the green.

questions.title: Dropping After Returning to Last Stroke Location
questions.question: If you decide to return to the spot of your last shot and declare your ball unplayable, how far from that spot are you allowed to drop your ball under the rules?
questions.explanation: You must drop the ball within one club-length of where your last shot was played, not closer to the hole.
